rv.q: This revival bids fair to be a must-see.
And yet, if there's a Shakespeare adaptation to be seen this summer, it's this one.
If “Henry VI” hasn’t proven as big a draw through the years, this juicy adaptation certainly presents a good argument for revisiting it more often.
In any case, I think the show deserves my tapping back into my initial youthful enthusiasm.
This production attempts to make that connection, but only succeeds half-way.
The production can do nothing with the plays’ shortcomings, though.
Five hours fly by in this gripping, emotionally rich adaptation.
The fight choreography, by Orlando Pabotoy and Kimiye Corwin is athletic and genuinely thrilling.

cn.t: Critics praise this ambitious NAATCO production for its gripping storytelling and vivid performances, with Shakespeare's rarely staged epic condensed into an emotionally rich, visually striking six-hour experience that brings the Wars of the Roses vividly to life.
